conversation_starters.title: Historic Carolina drought likely to end by October
conversation_starters.summary: A months-long, historically severe drought across the Carolinas began to ease after recent rainfall. As conditions improved, Iredell County (which includes the town of Troutman, north of Charlotte) was among 40 North Carolina counties moved into the least-severe Stage 1 drought category by the state Department of Environmental Quality. With the deficit shrinking, Troutman town officials lifted mandatory water restrictions and reopened the splash pad at ESC Park. Forecasters at the federal Climate Prediction Center then signaled the drought is likely to end by October.
conversation_starters.description: The Climate Prediction Center (CPC) has released the greatest news about the drought that the Carolinas have heard over the last several months.

you_should_know.title: Charlotte City Council faces I-77 South project decision deadline
you_should_know.summary: Charlotte's new mayor, Robert Harrington, took charge of the City Council at a consequential moment, inheriting divisive decisions. Two loomed largest: whether to proceed with toll lanes on Interstate 77 south of the city, and how to regulate the growth of data centers. As the story developed, attention narrowed to a pressing deadline for the council to decide on the I-77 South toll lane project, with data center rules still under discussion.

you_should_know.title: Duke Energy announces $2.6B in profits as state regulators deliberate on utility’s rate hike request
you_should_know.summary: Duke Energy, the region's electric utility, reported $2.6 billion in profits for the first half of the year—up nearly 12% from a year earlier—during a Tuesday earnings call. The results drew scrutiny because they came while state regulators were weighing the utility's request to raise customer rates; weeks earlier, its Carolinas division had partially scaled back that request and lowered its return-on-equity demand.

you_should_know.title: Thousands plan to rally against proposed hemp THC limits
you_should_know.summary: North Carolina lawmakers advanced House Bill 328, which would cap THC levels in hemp-derived products and set age requirements at the state level, ahead of federal limits due in late 2026. Businesses that make and sell these products warned the measure could wipe out legal operations and fuel a black market. As the House prepared to vote, thousands planned a rally in Raleigh, the state capital, to protest the proposed restrictions.
you_should_know.description: Hemp-derived THC manufacturers are planning a rally in Raleigh to protest House Bill 328, which seeks to impose state-level restrictions on THC content and age requirements before federal limits take effect in late 2026.
